mcqs.stem: A city levies $1,000,000 of property taxes for its fiscal year. It collects $900,000 during the year and expects to collect $40,000 within 60 days after year-end, $40,000 later in the next year, and $20,000 never. What property tax revenue does the **general fund** report?

choices.explanation: That is the accrual-basis amount reported in the government-wide statements.
Correct. Modified accrual recognizes amounts collected, or collectible within 60 days, as available.
That is cash-basis revenue; amounts collected within 60 days are also available.
Ignores both the availability criterion and the uncollectible amount.

mcqs.explanation: Governmental funds (modified accrual): revenue is measurable and available — collected within the period or soon enough (generally 60 days) to pay current liabilities: 900,000 + 40,000 = **$940,000**. The remaining $40,000 collectible is deferred inflows. Government-wide: 1,000,000 − 20,000 = 980,000.

lessonCitations.source: GASB Statement No. 34 (Basic Financial Statements and MD&A for State and Local Governments), as amended
GASB Statement No. 54 (Fund Balance Reporting and Governmental Fund Type Definitions)

mcqs.stem: At year-end Parent had a $75,000 receivable from Sub and Sub had a $75,000 payable to Parent. How is this reported in the consolidated balance sheet?

choices.explanation: An entity cannot owe itself; both are eliminated.
Correct. Intercompany receivables and payables are removed entirely.

choices.text: A net receivable of $0 disclosed as a related-party balance
choices.explanation: Eliminated intercompany balances are not related-party disclosures in consolidated statements.

choices.text: Only the NCI's share is eliminated
choices.explanation: Intercompany balances are eliminated 100%.

mcqs.explanation: Intercompany balances are eliminated in full on the consolidation worksheet (Dr Payable to Parent / Cr Receivable from Sub).

lessonCitations.note: Voting interest model; intercompany eliminations (810-10-45-1); NCI presentation

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 805-20 (Business Combinations — identifiable assets and liabilities)
lessonCitations.note: Acquisition-date measurement (detailed business-combination accounting is tested in BAR)

mcqs.stem: A researcher wants the paragraph explaining **when** a lessee first records a lease liability. Topic 842 (Leases), Subtopic 20 (Lessee). Which Codification section should she open?

choices.explanation: Section 30 covers initial measurement — the amount — not whether and when to record.
Correct. Section 25 is Recognition: whether and when an item is recorded.
Section 50 contains disclosure requirements.
Section 35 covers subsequent measurement after initial recording.

mcqs.explanation: Section numbers are consistent across all topics: -25 recognition, -30 initial measurement, -35 subsequent measurement, -45 presentation, -50 disclosure.

lessonCitations.note: Codification is the source of authoritative nongovernmental GAAP; SEC guidance for registrants

lessonCitations.source: FASB Concepts Statement No. 8, Chapter 1 (Objective) and Chapter 3 (Qualitative Characteristics)
FASB Concepts Statement No. 8, Chapter 4 (Elements of Financial Statements)

mcqs.stem: Where must a public company present diluted EPS?

choices.explanation: Basic and diluted EPS for continuing operations and net income are presented on the face.

choices.text: On the face of the income statement for income from continuing operations and net income
choices.explanation: Correct. Discontinued-operations EPS may be on the face or in the notes.

choices.text: In the statement of cash flows
choices.explanation: Cash flow per share is not permitted to be reported.

choices.text: Only when diluted EPS differs from basic by more than 3%
choices.explanation: There is no materiality threshold in the presentation requirement.

mcqs.explanation: ASC 260-10-45 requires basic and diluted EPS on the face of the income statement for income from continuing operations and net income, with equal prominence.

mcqs.stem: Net income was $300,000. During the year: unrealized gain on AFS debt securities $20,000; foreign currency translation loss $8,000; and dividends declared $50,000. All amounts are net of tax. What is comprehensive income?

choices.explanation: Dividends are distributions to owners, not part of comprehensive income.
This omits the translation loss.
The translation adjustment is a loss, not a gain.

mcqs.explanation: Comprehensive income = net income + OCI = 300,000 + 20,000 − 8,000 = **312,000**. Dividends are owner transactions, excluded from comprehensive income.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 220 (Income Statement — Reporting Comprehensive Income)
FASB ASC 225-20 (Unusual or infrequently occurring items)
FASB ASC 360-10-45 (Long-lived assets held for sale)

mcqs.stem: Which item is reported as a change in net assets **with** donor restrictions?

choices.text: A cash gift the donor stipulated must be used next year
choices.explanation: Correct. A time restriction makes it with donor restrictions until next year.
Expenses are reported only in net assets without donor restrictions.

choices.text: Board-designated funds for a future building
choices.explanation: Board designations are without donor restrictions.
Unrestricted revenue is without donor restrictions.

mcqs.explanation: Donor-imposed time or purpose restrictions create net assets with donor restrictions. Expenses and board designations never do.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 958-205 (Not-for-Profit Entities — Presentation), as amended by ASU 2016-14
FASB ASC 958-210 and 958-225 (Balance Sheet; Income Statement)
FASB ASC 958-720 (Other Expenses — functional and natural classification)

mcqs.stem: A state receives a $10 million donation whose principal must be kept intact; the earnings pay for maintenance of a public cemetery. Which fund type is used?

choices.explanation: Private-purpose trusts benefit individuals or outside organizations, not the government's own programs.
Correct. Principal kept intact; earnings support the government's programs.
Special revenue funds spend their resources; this principal must be kept intact.
Custodial funds hold resources for other parties.

mcqs.explanation: Permanent funds (governmental) report resources legally restricted so that only earnings may be used to support the government's programs.

lessonCitations.source: GASB Statement No. 34 (Basic Financial Statements and MD&A for State and Local Governments), as amended
GASB Statement No. 54 (Fund Balance Reporting and Governmental Fund Type Definitions)

mcqs.stem: Beginning retained earnings were $500,000. During the year, net income was $120,000, cash dividends declared were $40,000 (of which $10,000 was unpaid at year-end), and a prior-year error that understated expenses by $20,000 (pretax) was discovered. The tax rate is 25%. What is ending retained earnings?

choices.explanation: This ignores the prior-period adjustment.
This subtracts the correction pretax (20,000) instead of net of tax.
This deducts only the $30,000 of dividends paid; retained earnings drops when dividends are declared.

mcqs.explanation: Prior-period adjustment: understated expenses overstated prior income by 20,000 × (1 − 0.25) = **15,000** after tax, reducing opening RE. Ending RE = 500,000 − 15,000 + 120,000 − 40,000 declared = **565,000**.

lessonCitations.note: Current assets and current liabilities classification

mcqs.stem: During the year, a company paid $250,000 to a consulting firm owned by the brother of its CEO. At year-end it owed the firm $40,000. Which disclosure is most complete?

choices.text: The relationship (CEO's brother owns the firm), the nature of the consulting services, $250,000 of fees for the year, and $40,000 payable at year-end
choices.explanation: Correct. This covers relationship, description, amounts, and balances due.

choices.text: Only the $40,000 payable, as it is the balance sheet amount
choices.explanation: Transaction amounts for the period are also required.

choices.text: Only that the fees were at market rates
choices.explanation: Arm's-length claims need substantiation and do not replace the required disclosures.

choices.text: No disclosure, because consulting fees are ordinary-course expenses
choices.explanation: The ordinary-course exclusion covers compensation and expense allowances, not purchases from a relative's firm.

mcqs.explanation: Required elements: nature of the relationship, description of transactions, dollar amounts for each period, and amounts due to/from the related party.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 235-10 (Notes to Financial Statements — accounting policies)

mcqs.stem: A company's current ratio is 0.8. What effect will collecting $10,000 of accounts receivable have on the current ratio?

choices.explanation: Collecting receivables changes only the mix of current assets.
Neither total changes.
Correct. Cash rises and receivables fall by the same amount; total current assets are unchanged.
The effect is determinable — zero.

mcqs.explanation: Cash +10,000 and AR −10,000: total current assets and current liabilities are unchanged, so the current ratio stays 0.8. (The quick ratio is also unchanged — both are quick assets.)

lessonCitations.note: Users assess prospects for future net cash inflows; ratios are analytical tools, not GAAP requirements
Public companies discuss liquidity, capital resources, and results of operations, often using ratios

mcqs.stem: On January 1, Year 1, an investor bought $100,000 face, 8% five-year bonds (interest paid annually December 31) for $96,000, a 9% effective yield, classified as held-to-maturity. What is the carrying amount at December 31, Year 1?

choices.explanation: Uses straight-line amortization; the effective interest method is required when the result differs materially.
Ignores the discount amortization.
Subtracts the amortization; discount amortization increases the carrying amount.

mcqs.explanation: Interest revenue = 96,000 × 9% = 8,640; cash = 100,000 × 8% = 8,000; amortization = 640. Carrying amount = **$96,640**.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 326-20 and 326-30 (credit losses on HTM and AFS debt securities)

mcqs.stem: A FIFO company wrote inventory down from $90,000 cost to $78,000 NRV in Year 1. In Year 2, before any of the goods are sold, NRV recovers to $95,000. What is reported at the end of Year 2 (annual statements)?

choices.explanation: Inventory is never written above original cost.
U.S. GAAP prohibits reversing annual write-downs.
Correct. The written-down amount becomes the new cost basis.
There is no averaging of old and new values.

mcqs.explanation: Under U.S. GAAP, a write-down creates a new cost basis that is not written back up in later annual periods (IFRS would permit reversal up to original cost). Recoveries within the same fiscal year's interim periods are the exception.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 330-10-35 (Inventory — subsequent measurement, LCNRV and LCM)

mcqs.stem: A company assigns (pledges) its receivables as collateral for a bank loan. How are the receivables reported?

choices.explanation: Pledging is not a transfer of ownership.
Collateral is not netted against the debt.
They remain trade receivables.

choices.text: Kept on the balance sheet, with the pledge disclosed
choices.explanation: Correct. Pledged receivables remain the company's assets; the loan is recorded as a liability and the collateral arrangement is disclosed.

mcqs.explanation: Pledged receivables remain the company's assets; the loan is recorded as a liability and the collateral arrangement is disclosed.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 326-20 (Financial Instruments — Credit Losses, Measured at Amortized Cost)
FASB ASC 860-10-40 (Transfers and Servicing — derecognition conditions)

mcqs.stem: On July 1, Year 1, a company issued $600,000 of 10-year, 8% bonds at par, with interest payable annually each June 30. What interest payable is accrued on December 31, Year 1 (calendar year)?

choices.explanation: That's a full year.
Interest accrues with time.
That's 3 months.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 835-30 (Imputation of Interest; effective interest method and presentation of issuance costs)

mcqs.stem: At year-end, an AFS debt security has amortized cost of $150,000 and fair value of $158,000. Before adjustment, the fair value adjustment account had a $3,000 debit balance. What entry is required?

choices.text: Dr Fair value adjustment 8,000 / Cr OCI 8,000
choices.explanation: This ignores the existing 3,000 debit balance.

choices.text: Dr Fair value adjustment 5,000 / Cr OCI (unrealized gain) 5,000
choices.explanation: Correct. Required balance 8,000 debit − existing 3,000.

choices.text: Dr Fair value adjustment 5,000 / Cr Unrealized gain (net income) 5,000
choices.explanation: AFS changes go to OCI.
AFS securities are adjusted to fair value.

mcqs.explanation: Required adjustment balance = 158,000 − 150,000 = 8,000 debit. Existing 3,000 debit → adjust 5,000, credited to OCI.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 326-20 and 326-30 (credit losses on HTM and AFS debt securities)

mcqs.stem: Beginning inventory 200 units at $20; purchases of 300 units at $22 and then 250 units at $25. At year-end 350 units remain (periodic system). What is ending inventory under FIFO?

choices.explanation: This is LIFO ending inventory (200 × 20 + 150 × 22 = 7,300).
This is weighted average (16,850 ÷ 750 = 22.4667 × 350).
This values all 350 units at the latest $25 cost, but only 250 units were bought at $25.

mcqs.explanation: Goods available = 16,850 for 750 units. FIFO leaves the newest costs: 250 × $25 + 100 × $22 = **8,450**.

mcqs.stem: A company signs a 1-year, $50,000 note payable to a bank with interest at the market rate, paid at maturity. How is it initially recorded?

choices.explanation: Correct. A note bearing a market rate of interest is recorded at face.
Discounting applies when interest is below market or absent.
Interest accrues over time, not at issuance.
A borrowing is recorded when cash is received.

mcqs.explanation: When a note carries a reasonable market rate, face equals present value; interest is accrued as time passes.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 470-10-45 (classification of short-term obligations expected to be refinanced; callable debt)

mcqs.stem: Where is an unamortized bond discount reported?

choices.explanation: A discount is a contra-liability.

choices.text: As a reduction of bonds payable
choices.explanation: Correct. Bonds payable are reported net of unamortized discount (or plus unamortized premium).
It's amortized over the bond's life.
It's part of the debt's carrying amount.

mcqs.explanation: Bonds payable are reported net of unamortized discount (or plus unamortized premium).

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 835-30 (Imputation of Interest; effective interest method and presentation of issuance costs)

mcqs.stem: Beginning inventory 200 units at $20; purchases of 300 units at $22 and then 250 units at $25. At year-end 350 units remain (periodic system). What is ending inventory under the weighted-average method (rounded to the nearest dollar)?

choices.explanation: This uses a simple average of the three unit costs ($22.33) instead of weighting by units.
This is FIFO ending inventory, not weighted average.
This is LIFO ending inventory, not weighted average.

mcqs.explanation: Weighted-average cost = 16,850 ÷ 750 units = $22.4667. Ending inventory = 350 × 22.4667 = **7,863**.

mcqs.stem: A $5,000,000 construction contract is satisfied over time using cost-to-cost. Year 1 costs incurred were $1,200,000, with $2,800,000 estimated to complete. What gross profit is recognized in Year 1?

choices.explanation: That is total estimated gross profit, not Year 1's share.
Correct. 30% × $1,000,000 total gross profit.
Revenue over time is recognized as progress occurs.
That is Year 1 revenue, not gross profit.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 606-10-32 (Measurement — transaction price and allocation)
FASB ASC 606-10-25-23 to 25-37 (Satisfaction of performance obligations; over-time criteria)
FASB ASC 606-10-55-22 to 55-29 (Sale with a right of return)
FASB ASC 605-35-25-45 onward (provision for anticipated losses on construction-type contracts)
FASB ASC 340-40 (Other assets and deferred costs — contracts with customers)

mcqs.stem: A company expects to win a lawsuit and receive $1,500,000 in damages next year. What should it record?

choices.explanation: Gain contingencies aren't recognized before realization.

choices.text: Nothing in the accounts; disclosure is allowed if not misleading
choices.explanation: Correct. Gain contingencies are not recognized until realized or realizable (ASC 450-30).

choices.text: A receivable at the probability-weighted amount
choices.explanation: Gain contingencies aren't accrued.
No recognition.

mcqs.explanation: Gain contingencies are not recognized until realized or realizable (ASC 450-30).

mcqs.stem: A company has an NOL of $1,000,000 arising in the current year (federal, post-2017). The rate is 21%. Management concludes future taxable income is more likely than not to absorb it. What is recorded?

choices.text: A tax refund receivable of $210,000 from carryback
choices.explanation: Post-2017 federal NOLs generally can't be carried back.

choices.text: No tax benefit until the NOL is used
choices.explanation: A DTA is recognized now if realization is more likely than not.

choices.text: A DTA of $210,000 and a deferred tax benefit of $210,000
choices.explanation: Correct. Post-2017 NOLs carry forward indefinitely (usable up to 80% of taxable income each year).

choices.text: A DTA of $168,000, reflecting the 80% limitation
choices.explanation: The 80% limit affects timing of use, not the total DTA if fully realizable over time.

mcqs.explanation: Post-2017 NOLs carry forward indefinitely (usable up to 80% of taxable income each year). If realization is more likely than not, record a DTA of 1,000,000 × 21% = **210,000** with no valuation allowance.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 740-10-50-12 (rate reconciliation; expanded by ASU 2023-09)
Internal Revenue Code §11(b) (21% corporate rate) and §172 (NOL deduction limited to 80% of taxable income; indefinite carryforward)

mcqs.stem: Which situation requires revenue to be recognized **over time**?

choices.text: A retailer sells a television to a customer in a store
choices.explanation: Control transfers at a point in time.

choices.text: A cleaning company provides monthly office cleaning
choices.explanation: Correct. The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit.

choices.text: A manufacturer ships standard parts FOB shipping point
choices.explanation: Point in time at shipment.

choices.text: A developer sells a finished condominium unit
choices.explanation: Point in time when control passes.

mcqs.explanation: Routine services consumed as performed meet the first over-time criterion.

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 606-10-32 (Measurement — transaction price and allocation)
FASB ASC 606-10-25-23 to 25-37 (Satisfaction of performance obligations; over-time criteria)
FASB ASC 606-10-55-22 to 55-29 (Sale with a right of return)
FASB ASC 605-35-25-45 onward (provision for anticipated losses on construction-type contracts)
FASB ASC 340-40 (Other assets and deferred costs — contracts with customers)

mcqs.stem: A 4-year operating lease has payments of $30,000 at the end of each year; the liability is initially $104,000 (at 6%). What is the Year 1 lease cost?

choices.explanation: Correct. Straight-line: 120,000 ÷ 4.
This adds a year of interest (6,240) to the cash payment — mixing in finance-lease thinking.
That's the initial liability ÷ 4.
That's only the interest component.

mcqs.explanation: Operating lease cost = total payments 120,000 ÷ 4 years = **30,000** per year (interest 6,240 + ROU amortization 23,760).

lessonCitations.source: FASB ASC 842-20-25-6 and 35-3 (Operating lease subsequent measurement)

mcqs.stem: A company must value a liability at fair value. Which concept applies?

choices.text: The amount the company would pay to settle with the creditor today
choices.explanation: Fair value assumes transfer to a market participant, not settlement.

choices.text: The price that would be paid to transfer the liability to a market participant, reflecting nonperformance risk
choices.explanation: Correct. Fair value of a liability is a transfer price, and it reflects nonperformance risk (including the entity's own credit risk).
Fair value is a market-based present value.
That's historical, not fair value.

mcqs.explanation: Fair value of a liability is a transfer price, and it reflects nonperformance risk (including the entity's own credit risk).

tbs.title: Statement of cash flows — Lakeview Supply
tbs.instructions: Lakeview Supply uses the **indirect method**. Using the exhibits, complete the operating section and classify the listed transactions. Enter amounts as whole dollars; enter decreases in cash as negative numbers.

exhibits.title: Comparative balance sheet data
exhibits.content:
| Account | Dec 31, Year 1 | Dec 31, Year 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cash | 42,000 | 61,000 |
| Accounts receivable, net | 88,000 | 103,000 |
| Inventory | 130,000 | 118,000 |
| Prepaid insurance | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| Equipment | 400,000 | 440,000 |
| Accumulated depreciation | (160,000) | (170,000) |
| Accounts payable | 74,000 | 81,000 |
| Wages payable | 12,000 | 10,000 |
| Notes payable (long-term) | 150,000 | 120,000 |
| Common stock | 100,000 | 130,000 |
| Additional paid-in capital | 100,000 | 100,000 |
| Retained earnings | 70,000 | 120,000 |

exhibits.title: Year 2 additional information
exhibits.content:
- Net income for Year 2 was **$85,000**.
- Equipment with a cost of **$60,000** and accumulated depreciation of **$45,000** was sold for **$20,000** cash.
- New equipment was purchased for cash.
- Cash dividends of **$35,000** were declared and paid.
- Common stock was issued for cash.
- A note payable principal payment was made in cash.

rows.label: Depreciation expense
rows.explanation: Accumulated depreciation roll-forward: beginning 160,000 − 45,000 (removed on sale) + depreciation = ending 170,000, so depreciation = **55,000**. Add back.

rows.label: (Gain) or loss on sale of equipment
rows.explanation: Carrying amount 60,000 − 45,000 = 15,000; proceeds 20,000 → gain of 5,000. **Subtract** it (enter −5,000); the proceeds are investing.

rows.label: Change in inventory
rows.explanation: Inventory decreased 130,000 − 118,000 = 12,000 → add.

rows.label: Change in prepaid insurance
rows.explanation: Prepaid increased 3,000 → subtract.

rows.label: Change in accounts payable
rows.explanation: AP increased 7,000 → add.

rows.label: Change in wages payable
rows.explanation: Wages payable decreased 2,000 → subtract.

rows.label: Net cash provided by operating activities

parts.prompt: Compute the investing and financing amounts.

rows.label: Cash paid for new equipment
rows.explanation: Equipment roll-forward: 400,000 − 60,000 sold + purchases = 440,000 → purchases = **100,000**.

rows.label: Net change in cash (should agree with the balance sheets)
rows.explanation: 134,000 − 80,000 − 35,000 = **19,000**, which agrees with cash rising from 42,000 to 61,000.

parts.prompt: Classify each Year 2 item as it would appear in Lakeview's statement of cash flows.

rows.label: Dividends paid to shareholders
rows.explanation: Distributions to owners are financing.

rows.label: Interest paid on the note payable
rows.explanation: Interest paid is operating under U.S. GAAP.

rows.label: Proceeds from sale of equipment
rows.explanation: Full proceeds from PP&E sales are investing.

rows.label: Acquired a delivery van by signing a 3-year note to the dealer (no cash)
rows.explanation: Asset acquired with debt, no cash — disclose as a noncash investing and financing activity.

tbs.title: Bond investment amortization & classification — Lakeshore Insurance
tbs.instructions: On January 1, Year 1, Lakeshore Insurance bought Harper Corp. bonds: face **$400,000**, stated rate **5%** paid annually each December 31, maturing in 4 years. The market rate was **7%**, and Lakeshore paid **$372,902**. Use the effective interest method; round to whole dollars.

exhibits.title: Year-end fair values
exhibits.content:
| Date | Fair value of the Harper bonds |
|---|---:|
| Dec 31, Year 1 | 378,000 |
| Dec 31, Year 2 | 390,000 |

No credit losses are expected.

parts.prompt: Report the Year 1 amounts under each classification.

rows.label: If classified HTM — Dec 31, Year 1 balance sheet amount
rows.explanation: HTM is carried at amortized cost.

rows.label: If classified AFS — Dec 31, Year 1 balance sheet amount
rows.explanation: AFS is carried at fair value.

rows.label: If classified AFS — where does the Year 1 unrealized loss go?
rows.explanation: Non-credit unrealized losses on AFS debt securities go to OCI.

rows.label: If classified trading — where does the Year 1 unrealized loss go?
rows.explanation: Trading securities' fair value changes flow through net income.

parts.prompt: Assume AFS. Record the December 31, Year 2 fair value adjustment (a valuation account is used; its Year 1 balance was a $1,005 credit).
parts.explanation: Required Year 2 balance = 390,000 − 385,535 = 4,465 debit. Existing balance = 1,005 credit (378,000 − 379,005). Adjustment = 4,465 + 1,005 = **5,470** debit, credited to OCI.

tbs.title: Five-step revenue analysis — Clearwave Systems
tbs.instructions: Clearwave Systems (calendar year-end) signed two contracts during Year 1. Apply ASC 606 to determine performance obligations, allocate the transaction price, and compute Year 1 revenue.

exhibits.title: Contract 1 — Metro Hospital
exhibits.content:
Signed and delivered **October 1, Year 1**. Price: **$1,800,000**, due in 30 days.

| Promise | Standalone selling price |
|---|---:|
| Imaging hardware (works without Clearwave's installation) | 1,200,000 |
| Installation (standard; other firms offer it) — completed October 1 | 300,000 |
| 24 months of technical support starting October 1 | 500,000 |

The hardware comes with Clearwave's standard 1-year warranty against defects.

exhibits.title: Contract 2 — Delta Logistics
exhibits.content:
Consulting engagement completed **December 15, Year 1**. Fixed fee **$60,000** plus a performance bonus based on cost savings achieved, determined in March, Year 2:

| Bonus | Probability |
|---|---:|
| $20,000 | 50% |
| $10,000 | 30% |
| $0 | 20% |

Clearwave has extensive experience with similar contracts and concludes that including the estimate will not result in a significant reversal.

rows.label: Number of performance obligations
rows.explanation: Hardware, installation, and support are each distinct. The standard warranty is an assurance-type warranty — not a separate obligation.

rows.label: Standard 1-year warranty
rows.explanation: It only assures the hardware works as promised.

rows.label: Timing for the support revenue
rows.explanation: The customer simultaneously receives and consumes support as it's provided.

rows.label: Transaction price allocated to hardware
rows.explanation: 1,200,000 ÷ 2,000,000 × 1,800,000 = **1,080,000** (a 10% bundle discount spread proportionally).

rows.label: Contract liability at December 31, Year 1 (the customer paid in full in October)
Estimated bonus included in the transaction price
rows.explanation: Several possible outcomes → expected value: 0.5 × 20,000 + 0.3 × 10,000 + 0.2 × 0 = **13,000**.

rows.label: Contract 2 revenue for Year 1
rows.explanation: The service is complete, so recognize 60,000 + 13,000 = **73,000**; true up in Year 2 when the bonus is known.
